title: Normalized balanced scalar comparison of finite towers
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf{Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $A$ and uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale site of $W$, write $R_W=\varprojlim_n S_{W,n}$ and $S_{W,n}=(A/t^{n+1})_W$ with their specified projections and quotient transitions [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. The scheme and coefficient universes are independent. Use the functors $G$, $F_W$ (reductions), $H_W$ (koszuls), $D_g$ (diagramPull), $B_g$ (finite), and the predicates BalancedNormalization, QuotientUnitNormalization, KoszulNormalization, ReductionNormalization, with their literal section formulas, from [def-a1-finite-pullback-strict-tower-data]. These act on all unbounded cochain complexes of $R_W$-module sheaves; tensor products are the sheafified tensor and their signed direct-sum totalization [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. There exists a natural isomorphism $\lambda:F_X\circ G\cong B_g$ (in Lean functor order, $G\mathbin{\ggg}F_X$) such that for every complex $P$, BalancedNormalization holds for $\lambda_P$. Thus $(x\otimes b)\otimes1$ maps to the finite quotient-unit generator multiplied by $\pi_{X,n}(b)$, at every level and degree.

proof.text: Identify the inverse image of each finite coefficient sheaf with the target finite coefficient sheaf through the constant-preserving structural isomorphism. Its projection square commutes. Apply normalized inverse-image tensor comparison to identify the finite target with (g-inverse P tensor_D U_n) tensor_{U_n} V_n, retaining the adjunction-unit generators.

Apply the strict coefficient-square calculus to the projection square. Both scalar-extension orders identify with g-inverse P tensor_D V_n by multiplying the two coefficients after projection; their inverses insert 1. Balancing is exactly the projection square. The calculus supplies chain naturality and quotient-transition compatibility, so this is a natural isomorphism of the actual strict towers. Evaluating at the quotient unit gives precisely BalancedNormalization.

lean.statement:
theorem balanced_scalar_comparison :
    ∃ lambda : G l E g ⋙ reductions l E X ≅ finite l E g,
      ∀ P : CochainComplex (Modules l E Y) ℤ,
        BalancedNormalization l E g P (lambda.app P)
